Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate with a matching frame cap gives the smoothest feel the Deck can reliably sustain in open-world and light multiplayer scenarios; drop shadows to Low to reclaim GPU headroom. Crowded PvP or town areas may dip to the low 30s.

profiles.Summary: New World: Aeternum is a demanding online action RPG whose PC minimum GPU sits around GTX 1060 class — a step above the Steam Deck's roughly GTX 1050 Ti equivalent — meaning the Deck needs low settings, reduced resolution, and FSR to stay playable. The game is Steam Deck Verified as Playable and runs under Proton, but as an online-only MMO it requires a stable internet connection and may have occasional server-side performance hiccups.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1060 target, just above the Deck's GPU class) and Steam Deck hardware capabilities. On your first session, check frame rate in a populated town — if it drops below 25 fps consistently, switch to the Max Battery profile and lower Texture Quality to Low.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU well within the 8 W TDP envelope; expect dips in crowded towns but generally stable solo/small-group content. Disable VSync in-game and rely on the Deck's frame limiter instead.

KnownIssues: Online-only: requires a persistent internet connection; no offline play possible on Deck.
ProtonDB trending gold/silver suggests some players hit stability or launch issues under Proton — GE-Proton may improve compatibility.
High VRAM/RAM pressure from shared 16 GB pool can cause stutters in crowded areas (towns, PvP zones).
In-game UI and text can be very small at 1280x800; use the game's Adjustable Text Size feature.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at native 1280x800 with all power unlocked squeezes the most frames out of the Deck, but the GPU is the hard bottleneck; a 45 fps cap prevents fruitless chasing of 60 fps and reduces heat. Battery life is short — keep a charger handy.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh and frame cap delivers a smooth, tear-free experience at a reasonable power draw; FSR at 1024x640 keeps the image acceptable while giving the GPU headroom. Performance may dip to the low 30s in the busiest town areas.

profiles.Summary: New World: Aeternum is a demanding open-world MMO that significantly exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities at native resolution, requiring low settings and FSR upscaling to achieve a playable frame rate. Expect 30–40 fps in open areas with performance dropping noticeably in towns, trading posts, and large-scale PvP events.
profiles.BasisNote: No dedicated Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements and Steam Deck hardware class. On your first run, check frame rate in a busy town — if it drops below 25 fps consistently, switch to the Max Battery profile and lower View Distance further.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and an 8 W TDP cap maximises battery life; expect dips below 30 fps in towns and war zones. Avoid large group content in this profile as performance will struggle to stay playable.

KnownIssues: Performance drops significantly in towns, trading posts, and large-scale war/PvP events, making a stable 30 fps difficult to maintain in those scenarios.
ProtonDB trending gold/silver suggests some users encounter launcher issues, crashes, or input quirks under Proton — GE-Proton is commonly recommended.
Controller support is not officially confirmed; UI and prompts may be optimised for mouse and keyboard, requiring workarounds on Deck.
An always-on internet connection is required; any network interruption will immediately disconnect you from the session.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Pushing the TDP to 15 W and GPU clock to max extracts the most the Deck can realistically offer; expect drops into the mid-30s in towns and war events even at these settings. Battery life will be short, so best suited for plugged-in or short sessions.
